prompt: Wrap text to a column width without splitting words. Complete the wrap method so it returns the lines, each at most width characters long.
explanation: Greedy word wrapping keeps a StringBuilder for the line being built: a word joins the current line only when the existing length plus one space plus the word still fits. Otherwise the finished line is pushed and the word starts a fresh one, which is also why an over-long word ends up alone. Splitting on the regex \s+ after trim() collapses runs of whitespace, and the final non-empty line must be flushed after the loop.
hints: text.trim().split("\\s+") gives you the words with all runs of whitespace collapsed.
Track the line you are building in a StringBuilder; a word fits when line.length() + 1 + word.length() <= width.
When a word does not fit, add the current line to the list, reset the builder, and start it with that word -- then remember to add whatever is left after the loop ends.
